# Parental controls

Parental controls allow you to view and manage your child’s experience on Roblox. These controls are available for parents of children in **Roblox Kids** and **Roblox Select** accounts.

## How to set-up your parental account

[Create account](https://www.roblox.com/)

### Step 1:

Help your child navigate to the **Parental controls** tab in their Roblox account **Settings**.

### Step 2:

Click **Add parent**. Type in your email address where prompted. This will trigger an email with instructions for creating and linking your account.

### Step 3:

Follow the instructions in the email that was sent to your inbox. If you’re new to Roblox, **create an account**. Be sure to have a government-issued ID ready to verify your identity.

### Step 4:

Once your account is created, you’ll see a prompt asking if you want to link your account to your child’s. Click **Agree**. This will give you access to parental controls for their account.

![](https://cms-media.roblox.com/assets/f5385d1a-870a-3256-5f56-9c480dc98a77.webp)

How to set up your parental account (via email)

Once you’ve created an account, make sure you have the email associated with that account open.

First, you’ll need your child to send you an account linking request

1. Have your child log into their account
2. Go to **settings** and navigate to **Parental Controls**
3. Click the **Add parent** button
4. Have them enter the email address associated with your account

Now you’re ready to link your accounts!

1. Open the email you received from your child’s Roblox account
2. Select **use existing account**to log in
3. Follow the onscreen steps to verify your age using a government-issued ID or credit card. Learn more about Age ID verification.

After verifying your age, the page will automatically refresh. Select **Agree** to link to your child’s account, and you’ll be able to approve certain actions for your child.

How to set up your parental account (via settings)

You can also link your Roblox account on your child’s Roblox account [settings](https://www.roblox.com/my/account#!/info).

1. Go to **Settings**
   1. On desktop: Select the **gear** **icon** located at the top right
   2. On mobile: Select **More** located at the bottom right, and select **Settings** (gear icon)
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**, and select **Add** **parent**
3. Follow the onscreen steps to verify your age using a government-issued ID or credit card. After verifying your age, the page will automatically refresh.
4. Select **Agree** to link to your child’s account. Learn more about [ID verification](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407282410644).

Unlinking from your child’s account

To unlink a child’s account from your account, go to **Settings > Parental Controls**, and select the child you want to unlink from. Select the **pencil icon** in the top right corner, and then select **Unlink** accounts. Note that if you unlink your account from your child’s, you will no longer be able to provide permission for actions on Roblox, control their privacy settings, and set screen time or spending limits.

## What can parents manage on Roblox?

In most regions, parents can manage all settings through the age of 12. Certain controls (i.e., game management and Direct Chat) can be managed through the age of 15.

[### Content

Choose the content maturity level for your child’s account.

Learn more](/parental-controls#manage-game-maturity-ratings)[### Chat & connections

Manage how your child communicates on our platform and review who they’re connecting with.

Learn more](/parental-controls#manage-chat-settings-on-roblox)[### Screen time

Monitor and manage how much time your child spends on our platform.

Learn more](/parental-controls#manage-screen-time)[### Spending

Set monthly spending limits and enable notifications to monitor your child’s spending.

Learn more](/parental-controls#set-up-spending-limits)

## More for parents

We know how complex the online world can be, especially for parents of younger children. On top of our Roblox Kids and Select accounts, we’ve created online resources, in partnership with safety experts, to help you navigate digital safety with your children.

[Learn more](/parent-resources)

## How to set up parental controls

Access the following controls by navigating to **Settings > Parental Controls** in your account. See below for detailed instructions.

Manage game maturity ratings

![](https://cms-media.roblox.com/assets/6aef6356-3866-d589-f607-025805f9d3ff.webp)

You can use the content maturity settings to adjust our default maturity restrictions in Roblox Kids and for users under 13 in Roblox Select accounts. This allows you to customize your child’s experience based on their personal sensitivity levels.

* Go to **Settings**
* Go to **Parental controls** and select your child's account
* Go to **Settings you manage**
* Scroll down to Settings you manage and select **Content restrictions**
* Select **Content maturity**
* Adjust the slider bar to the right or left to select the content maturity level that you are comfortable with.  A brief description of the type of content will appear below the selected setting. Note that Restricted experiences are only available to 18+ verified users.

Block a game

You can block a game from your child’s Roblox Kids or Roblox Select account to prevent them from playing it, regardless of its content maturity rating.

Block an experience to prevent your child from accessing it, regardless of its content maturity level. Blocked experiences will still appear in search results. To block an experience:

1. Go to Settings
   * On desktop: Select the gear icon located at the top right
   * On mobile: Select More located at the bottom right, and select Settings (gear icon)
2. Go to Parental controls and select your child's account
3. Scroll down to Settings you manage and select Content restrictions
4. Select Blocked games
5. Select the + icon. In the search bar, type the experience name you want to block.
6. Select Block and confirm.
7. To unblock an experience, click Unblock and confirm.

Note: If you block a game while your child is playing, the block will only take effect the next time they enter the game.

Allow a game

To allow a game your child has requested

1. Navigate to your **Settings** and click the **Parental controls** tab
2. Choose the linked child’s account that you’d like manage
3. View **pending requests** in that child’s dashboard
4. Click **Allow** or Don’t Allow

Remove content with sensitive issues

The sensitive issues content label is applied to experiences that are primarily themed on current sensitive social, political, or religious issues. This descriptor is not intended to take a stance on any of these issues. By default, users under 13 cannot access experiences that are primarily themed on sensitive issues. To enable access for your child:

1. Go to **Settings.**
   * On desktop: Select the **gear icon** located at the top right.
   * On mobile: Select **More** located at the bottom right, and select **Settings** (gear icon).
2. Go to **Parental Controls** and select your child’s account.
3. Go to **Settings you manage** and select **Content restrictions**.
4. Select **Sensitive issues.**
5. Toggle the **Allow sensitive issues** selector ON to allow your child to access experiences that are primarily themed on sensitive issues.

**Note:**You can toggle the selector OFF at any time to disable their access.

Manage chat settings on Roblox

Communication controls allow you to determine who your child can chat with on Roblox. To access chat features, every user **must** [**complete an age check**](https://about.roblox.com/age-estimation)**.**

This will unlock [default age group settings](https://about.roblox.com/safety-by-age). You can adjust these settings by following the instructions below. Parents can choose to turn chat off for users under 13.

Note: If you decide to allow your child under 9 to chat, they will only be able to communicate with users under 13 years old or [trusted friends](https://about.roblox.com/safety-faqs#trusted-friends).

**Experience Chat.**Experience Chat is our in-game messaging feature that allows users to communicate while playing.

1. Go to **Settings**
   1. On desktop: Select the gear icon located at the top right
   2. On mobile: Select More located at the bottom right, and select Settings (gear icon)
2. Go to **Parental Controls**
3. Scroll down to Settings you manage and select **Communication**
4. Select **Experience chat** (in-game chat).
5. Choose if your child can use Experience chat with everyone in the game or no one by following these steps.
   1. **Experience chat** - This is the setting for Roblox’s real-time, in-game chat feature that is publicly visible for everyone in the game. It does not apply to chat features created independently by creators for their games. Choose to turn Experience Chat **on** or **off.**
6. **Direct chat** - This is the setting that determines who your child can chat with one-on-one in games (not publicly visible to everyone). This setting does not apply to chat features that were independently developed by creators. Choose to turn Direct Experience Chat **on** or **off**.

**Chat with Friends.** Roblox's Chat Tab allows users to start conversations with friends and [trusted friends](/safety-faqs) at any time. This way, users can decide what game they want to play together, jump in and play, and then talk about the game when they’re done, all in the same place.

The Chat Tab is only available for users 9+. Parents can enable this Chat Tab for their children ages 9-15 who have a Roblox Select account. For users ages 9-12, it is only available with trusted friends. For users 13-15, parents can turn on the Chat tab with trusted friends and friends who are age-appropriate (see Roblox age groups here).

**How to turn on Chat with Friends.**

1. Return to **Communication** in your **Parental Controls**.
2. Select **Chat and party with friends.** If your child is age 9-12, you can choose allow them to start chats with trusted friends. If your child is age 13-15 you can choose between only trusted friends or all friends.
   1. From **Chat and party with friends**, you can update the setting to all friends, trusted friends, or no one.

**Voice Chat** **with friends.** This setting is only available in some regions. It is only available with trusted friends for users under 18 years old.

Voice Chat with friends allows users to call friends anytime on the platform. This allows users to discuss games hands-free with friends and trusted friends.

Voice chat with friends is OFF for all users under 13. Parents can choose enable voice chat with [trusted friends](/safety-faqs) for users 9-12. Voice chat is ON for users ages 13-15 with trusted friends. Parents can choose to turn this off.

**How to enable or disable Voice chat with friends:**

1. Return to **Communication** in your **Parental Controls**.
2. Select **Chat and party with friends**
3. Scroll to the **Voice Chat with friends section**
4. Choose **Trusted friends** or **No one**

Review private servers

A private server is a Roblox experience with limits on who can join. To limit who can join your child’s private servers, and whose servers they can join:

1. Go to **Settings**.
   * On desktop: Select the **gear icon** located at the top right.
   * On mobile: Select **More** located at the bottom right, and select **Settings** (gear icon).
2. Go to **Parental Controls**.
3. Go to **Settings you manage** and select **Visibility & private servers**.
4. Go to **Private servers**.

Choose between **Connections** or **No one**.

Set up spending limits

**Set Up Monthly Spending Limits**

You can set a monthly limit on how much money your child can spend on Roblox, including Robux or subscriptions to individual experiences. This limit does not impact gift card redemption. You can also choose to enable or disable notifications about your child's spending.

To set spending controls:

1. Go to **Settings.**
   1. On desktop: Select the gear icon located at the top right.
   2. On mobile: Select More located at the bottom right, and select Settings (gear icon).
2. Go to **Parental Controls.**
3. Go to Settings You Manage and select **Spending restrictions.**
4. Set a Monthly spending limit. Regardless of whether the allowed monthly limit is reached, it will reset at the end of the calendar month and not roll over.
5. You can also determine if you want to receive spending notifications. You can choose if you want to be notified for all transactions, high spend alerts, or none. High spend notifications are on by default for all linked parents. This means that you should receive purchase notifications after $100, $250, and $500 of spend in a given month (or the equivalent in local currency). After reaching $500, you should receive purchase notifications for every ten transactions.

Learn more in the Monthly Spending Limits help article.

**Inventory visibility**

You can control who can see your child's inventory, which includes items purchased or traded with other users.

To set inventory visibility:

1. Go to **Settings.**
   1. On desktop: Select the gear icon located at the top right.
   2. On mobile: Select More located at the bottom right, and select Settings (gear icon).
2. Go to **Parental Controls.**
3. Go to Settings You Manage.
4. Go to **Trading & inventory.**
5. Select between Everyone, Connections, or No one.

**Trading (Premium &** [**Plus**](https://www.roblox.com/plus) **only)**

Users with a [Roblox Plus](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/47967913158164-Roblox-Plus) or Premium subscription can trade Limited items with other members.

To disable trading and set limits on who your child can trade with:

1. Go to Settings.
   1. On desktop: Select the gear icon located at the top right.
   2. On mobile: Select More located at the bottom right, and select Settings (gear icon).
2. Go to Parental Controls.
3. Go to Settings you manage.
4. Go to Trading & inventory.
5. Select between Friends or No one.

**Send and Get Robux**

[Roblox Plus subscribers](https://www.roblox.com/plus) can transfer Robux to others. To help keep transfers secure, parent or caregiver approval is required every time younger users send or receive Robux. Users must be age-checked and 18+ before they can send or receive without parental approval. Transfers are also subject to:

* A daily limit of 500 Robux max
* A monthly limit of 1000 Robux max
* Fraud checks - transfers will only proceed if all eligibility, safety, and limit requirements are met. These safety requirements may continue to evolve over time, including to reflect regional requirements.

Review friends list

You can view, block, and report your child’s Roblox Connections from within parental controls.

To manage your child’s Connections list:

1. Go to **Settings**.
   * On desktop: Select the **gear icon** located at the top right.
   * On mobile: Select **More** located at the bottom right, and select **Settings** (gear icon).
2. Go to **Parental Controls**.
3. Scroll down to **Connections** and select **Manage**.
4. Your child's Connections will be displayed as usernames alongside their avatar. You can click on an avatar to see the user's profile.
5. You can block and report a Connection by selecting the three dot menu next to the username. Select **Block** and confirm to remove the user from your child’s connections.

Blocked users will not be able to chat directly with your child or add them as a Connection again without your permission. Select **Report** to file a complaint against the user.

Manage screen time

Screen time limits allow you to restrict the amount of time that your child is permitted to spend on Roblox each day. This is available for all users in Roblox Kids accounts and users ages 9-12 in Roblox Select accounts. For 13+ Roblox Select and Roblox users we suggest parents have conversations about the effects of too much screentime and setting limits for themselves.

Once they reach their limit, your child will see a message explaining that they have hit their limit, and they will no longer be able to use Roblox for the rest of the day.

Unlink your account from your child’s

To unlink a child’s account from your account, go to **Settings** > **Parental Controls**, and select the child you want to unlink from. Select the pencil icon in the top right corner, and then select Unlink accounts. Note that if you unlink your account from your child’s, you will no longer be able to provide permission for actions on Roblox, control their privacy settings, and set screen time or spending limits.

Approving a trusted friend for your under 13 child

If your child is under 13 years old, trusted friends can only be added with your permission.

You will receive a request from us via email or as a pending request in your Parental Controls.

You have 24 hours to select ‘Approve’ from either. If you miss the 24 hour window, your child can resend the request.

# Parental Controls Overview

Roblox offers a variety of parental controls to help parents and caregivers manage their child’s game on the platform. You will need a Roblox account linked to your child’s account to manage parental controls on behalf of your child. Learn more in the [Parents: How to Link Your Child’s Account](/hc/en-us/articles/30428321333140) help article.

## Content Controls

The content maturity settings allow you to control the types of content your child has access to in Roblox games. To adjust your child’s setting:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls** and select your child's account
3. Go to **Settings** **you** **Manage**
4. Scroll down to **Settings** **you** **manage** and select **Content** **restrictions**
5. Select **Content maturity**
6. Adjust the slider bar to the right or left to select the content maturity level that you are comfortable with. A brief description of the type of content will appear below the selected setting. Note that Restricted games are only available to 18+ age checked users.

## Allowed and Blocked Games

Roblox Kids and Roblox Select accounts only provide access to a set of age-appropriate games. Use specific game controls to manage whether your child can access individual games in Roblox Kids or Roblox Select.

**Allow a game**

If a game is not available by default in your child’s Roblox Kids or Roblox Select account, you are able to allow access to that specific game.

Email

1. Select **View Settings** in the request email to open the request in Roblox.
2. Select **Allow** or **Don’t Allow** to approve or deny the request.

Parental Controls

1. Navigate to **Pending requests** in your settings to see any allowed games requests.
2. Select **Allow** or **Don’t Allow** to approve or deny the request.
3. Review and manage your child’s allowed games via **Content restrictions** > **Allowed games**.
   * To revoke approval for a game, select the **three-dot menu** next to the game title and select **Don’t allow**.

**Block a game**

Block a game to prevent your child from accessing it, regardless of its content maturity level. Blocked games will still appear in search results. To block a game:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls** and select your child's account
3. Scroll down to **Settings** **you** **manage** and select **Content** **restrictions**
4. Select **Blocked** **games**
5. Select the **+** icon. In the search bar, type the game name you want to block
6. Select **Block** and confirm. To unblock a game, click Unblock and confirm.
   * *If you block a game while your child is playing, the block will only take effect the next time they enter the game.*

## Content Labels

Our content maturity labels help users and their parents understand what types of content to expect in Roblox games. These labels are grounded in child development research and informed by industry standards. Parents can use the content maturity setting in parental controls to restrict their child’s access to content based on what makes sense for their family.

### Content Label Descriptions

* **Minimal:** May contain occasional mild violence, light unrealistic blood, and/or occasional mild fear.
* **Mild:** May contain repeated mild violence, heavy unrealistic blood, mild crude humor, and/or repeated mild fear.
* **Moderate:** May contain moderate violence, light realistic blood, moderate crude humor, unplayable gambling content, and/or moderate fear.
* **Restricted:** May contain strong violence, heavy realistic blood, moderate crude humor, romantic themes, unplayable gambling content, the presence of alcohol, strong language, and/or moderate fear. We allow access to Restricted content only for users who are 17+ age-verified.

## Sensitive Issues

The sensitive issues content label is applied to games that are primarily themed on current sensitive social, political, or religious issues. This descriptor is not intended to take a stance on any of these issues. By default, users under 13 cannot access games that are primarily themed on sensitive issues. To enable access for your child:

1. Go to **Settings**.
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls** and select your child's account.
3. Go to **Settings** **you** **Manage**.
4. Scroll down to **Settings** **you** **manage** and select **Content** **restrictions**.
5. Select **Sensitive issues**.
6. Toggle the **Allow sensitive issues** selector ON to allow your child to access games that are primarily themed on sensitive issues.
   * *You can toggle the selector OFF at any time to disable their access.*

## Communication Controls

Communication controls allow you to determine how your child can chat on Roblox.

If your child has completed an age check, you can edit your child’s communication settings to determine how your child can use text chat.

To set the controls for **Game chat**:

1. Go to **Settings**.
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**.
3. Scroll down to **Settings** **you** **manage** and select **Communication**.
4. Go to **Communication**. There are multiple settings:
   * **Game** **chat**: Game chat allows your child to chat with other users in similar age groups within a specific game.
     1. **Game chat**: This determines if your child can text chat with users in similar age groups in the same game. You can find more info on game chat here.  Users under the age of 9 require parental consent to enable game chat.
     2. **Game direct chat**: This determines who your child can chat with directly when using the ‘/w’ command inside of a game server. Users can only direct chat with other age checked users in similar age groups. Users under the age of 13 require parental consent to enable direct chat.
   * **Friends chat**:This determines if your child can text chat with users they have added as friends on Roblox.

*Note: These settings do not apply to chat features developed independently by developers.*

Party chat is only allowed between age checked users above 13 in similar age groups. To use parental controls for **Party**:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**
3. Scroll down to **Settings** you **manage** and select **Communication**
4. Go to **Communication**
5. Select **Party**. A Party allows you to group up to join games together.
6. Select options for each of the settings to determine who can join parties with your child. There are two settings available:
   * **Party**: You have the option to change the Party setting from **Friends** to **No one**. Selecting **Friends** limits you to a 1:1 Party (up to two members), and if you select **No one**, you will be unable to participate in any Party.
   * **Group Party**: You also have the option to change the Group Party setting from **Friends** to **No one**. When **Friends** is selected, you can be in a Party with up to six members.

## Private Servers

A private server is a Roblox game with limits on who can join. To limit who can join your child’s private servers and whose servers they can join:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**
3. Scroll down to **Settings** **you** **manage** and select **Visibility** **&** **private** **servers**
4. Select **Private** **Servers**
5. Choose between **Friends** or **Off**

## Friends List

You can view, block, and report your child’s Roblox friends from within your parent dashboard. To manage your child’s friends list:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**
3. Scroll down to **Friends** and select **Manage**
4. Your child’s friend will be displayed as usernames alongside their avatar. You can select an avatar to see the user’s profile.
5. You can block and report a friend by selecting the three-dot menu next to the friend. Select **Block** and confirm to remove the user from your child’s friend list.
6. Blocked users will not be able to chat directly with your child or add them as a friend again without your permission. Select **Report** to file a complaint against the user.

## Spending Controls

You can set a monthly spending limit on how much money your child can spend on Roblox, including Robux or subscriptions to individual games. This limit does not impact gift card redemption. You can also choose to enable or disable notifications about your child’s spending.

To set spending controls:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**
3. Go to **Settings** **You** **Manage**
4. Scroll down to Settings you manage and select **Spending** **restrictions**
5. You can set a monthly spending limit. Regardless of whether the allowed monthly limit is reached, it will reset at the end of the calendar month and not roll over.
6. You can also determine if you want to receive spending notifications. You can choose if you want to be notified for every transaction, for only very high monthly spending, or both. High spend notifications are on by default for all linked parents. This means that you should receive purchase notifications after $100, $250, and $500 of spend in a given month (or the equivalent in local currency). After reaching $500, you should receive purchase notifications for every ten transactions by default.

Learn more in the [Monthly Spending Limits](/hc/en-us/articles/4409125091348) help article.

## Robux Balance

You can view your child's Robux balance and add Robux to their account from Parental Controls. This is available for all children linked to your account.

**View your child's Robux balance**

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental Controls** and select your child's account
3. Scroll down to **Robux**. Your child's current Robux balance is shown.

**Add Robux to your child's account**

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental Controls** and select your child's account
3. Scroll down to **Robux** and select **Add Robux**

## Screen Time Controls

Screen time controls allow you to restrict the amount of time that your child is allowed to spend on Roblox each day. Once they reach their limit, your child will see a message explaining that they have hit their limit, and they will no longer be able to use Roblox for the rest of the day. To set screen time controls:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**
3. Scroll down to **Screen** **time** and select **Manage** next to the chart at the top of the screen, which shows a seven-day average for screen time
4. Select **Screen** **time** **limit**
5. Select a time limit in the **Daily** **limit** dropdown

You can also view your child’s Roblox top 20 games played from the last week. To view top games played:

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Go to **Parental** **Controls**
3. Scroll down to **Screen** **time** and select **Manage**
4. Select **Top** **games**

Learn more in the [Managing Screen Time](/hc/en-us/articles/30428328969492) help article.

### Get quick help with Ask Internet Matters

Discover our AI-powered assistant

# Roblox parental controls

## Step-by-step guide

![Roblox privacy controls guide hero](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/roblox-new-logo-2-300x158.png)

## What you need to know

[Learn more about the app.](/advice/apps-and-platforms/online-gaming/roblox/)

## Quick advice

Set up Roblox parental controls to keep your child safe while they game.

### Set content restrictions

Customise the automatic content restrictions for under-13s to help curate games and experiences for their interests and maturity.

### Manage chat settings

Customise communication settings so that only your child’s friends can contact them. You can also set quick language filters.

### Manage spending

Set monthly spending restrictions in Roblox and receive spend notifications to avoid accidental overspending in games.

## Video guide

![A few people holding their devices with a logo inside it representing Internet Matters' artificial intelligence assistant. Text reads: Ask Internet Matters](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/hero-ask-internet-matters-300x158.webp)

### Need a quick answer?

Ask our AI assistant about devices, apps and games.

## How to set Roblox parental controls

The following steps were recreated using an Android device. While the steps work across other devices, you might notice some visual differences from the screenshots below.  
  
You will need access to your child’s account for Roblox and the system they play on.

### How to set up a parent account

To use Roblox parental controls, you must set up a parent account. You can then link your child’s account to yours for access to a range of settings and insights.

#### To create a parent account:

**Step 1** – If you already have a Roblox account, great! If not, you can [register here](https://www.roblox.com/CreateAccount). In the Roblox app ([Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.roblox.client&hl=en_GB), [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/roblox/id431946152)), tap **More** > **Settings** > **Account Info**.

![Screenshot of a Roblox account and menu with Settings selected.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parent-account-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – Under **Email Address**, add your **parent email**. This is the same email you’ll need to enter to connect your child’s account to yours. Check your email to **verify your account**.

![Screenshot of Account Info screen with Email Address highlighted.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parent-account-2-291x300.webp)

**Step 3** – Under **Birthday**, tap **Verify My Age**. Choose either the **credit card** route or the **photo ID** route.

Follow the instructions on screen to complete the process, which should only take a minute or two.

You can [learn how age checks protect your privacy with this guide](/resources/uk-age-verification-law-for-pornography-sites-explained-parent-guide/).

![Screenshot of Account Info screen on Roblox showing the start of the parent age verification process.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parent-account-3-291x300.webp)

Your Roblox parent account is now ready to link to your child’s for use of parental controls.

### Linking your account to your child’s

If your child is under the age of 13, you can set parental controls across their account. To do this, you must link your Roblox parent account to your child’s account.

#### To link to your child’s account:

**Step 1** – On **your child’s account**, tap on **More** > **Settings** > **Account Info**. Tap **Add parental recovery email**.

Enter the email you use for your own Roblox account. **Check your email** to confirm.

![Screenshot showing where to add a parent email on a child's Roblox account.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parental-controls-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – Return to the **Settings** menu on your child’s Roblox account. Tap **Parental Controls** > **Add Parent**. Enter **your email**.

![Screenshot showing parental controls setup in Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parental-controls-2-291x300.webp)

**Step 3**– Check **your email** to confirm the link. If you still don’t have an account, select Create account. Otherwise, select **Use existing account** and **login**. Then, tap **Agree**.

![Screenshot showing the final steps of linking a parent account on Roblox to a child account.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parental-controls-3-291x300.webp)

Note: If you have not verified your age, you will be asked to do so before you can link to your child’s account.

Otherwise, you can return to **your Roblox account** to customise parental controls for your child.

### Verify your child’s age

When your child opens Roblox, they will be asked to verify their age. Through facial estimation, Roblox can assign your child to an age-based account. Learn [how age-based accounts work.](/advice/apps-and-platforms/online-gaming/roblox/#anchor-block-e96e24eea14d148d44bbd77a7be0a0a1)

#### To verify your child’s age:

**Step 1 –** Open your child’s Roblox app and click **Continue** in the age check popup.

**Step 2** – On the next page, select **Continue**.

![Roblox age verification 1](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-age-verification-1-275x300.webp)

**Step 3** – Click **Continue.**

**Step 4** – Give Roblox permission to use the camera.

![Roblox age verification 2](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-age-verification-2-275x300.webp)

**Step 5** – Have your child follow the instructions on the screen to complete facial estimation.

**Step 6** – You will receive the estimated age group. If this is wrong, select **Continue with ID** to give proof of your child’s real age. If it is correct, select **Continue**.

Your child’s age is now verified, and they will only be able to interact with users within the same age group.

![Roblox age verification 3](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-age-verification-3-275x300.webp)

### How to manage screen time on Roblox

Roblox has a lot of fun games and experiences that children enjoy. Unfortunately, children can struggle to switch off and take breaks, so Roblox has in-built screen time controls parents can use.

#### To set screen time limits:

**Step 1** – When logged into **your parent account** in the Roblox app, tap **More** > **Settings** > **Parental Controls**. Next to **Screen time**, tap **Manage**.

![Screenshot of Roblox parental controls with screen time highlighted.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-screen-time-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – Tap **Screen time limit**. Under **Daily limit**, tap the **dropdown box** and choose a **limit**.

There are a range of options from 15 minutes to over 3 hours. Choose the maximum amount of time you want to allow each day. We recommend limiting it to 1 hour at most to encourage balance with other activities both online and offline.

![Screenshot of Roblox screen time limits menu.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-screen-time-2-291x300.webp)

Under Screen time, you can also view Top experiences to see which games your child plays the most on Roblox. This is a great tool to help you [talk with them about their online life](/resources/guide-to-encourage-kids-to-share-their-digital-lives/).

### Where can you set content restrictions?

With Roblox parental controls, you can set [maturity levels](#maturity) and [block specific experiences](#block-experience) within those levels.

#### To set maturtiy levels:

**Step 1** – Under **More** > **Settings** > **Parental controls**, scroll down and tap **Content restrictions**.

![Screenshot of Roblox parental controls menu with Content restrictions highlighted.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-content-restriction-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2**– Tap **Content maturity**. Set your child’s **Content maturity level**, choosing between **Minimal**, **Mild** and **Moderate**. You cannot choose Restricted for under-13s because certain content is already restricted for this age group.

**Minimal** is the best option for younger children or those who might struggle to process content which is violent, bloody or scary even if it’s not realistic.

![Screenshot showing how to set content maturity level on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-content-restriction-2-291x300.webp)

#### To block specific experiences:

**Step 1** – From the **Content restrictions** screen, tap **Blocked experiences**. Next to **Blocked experiences**, tap the **+ symbol**.

![Screenshot showing where to block specific experiences on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-content-restriction-3-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – Search for the full experience **title or a keyword** within the title. When you see the correct experience, tap **Block** beneath the image. Tap **Block** again to confirm.

![Screenshot showing the process of blocking an experience on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-content-restriction-4-291x300.webp)

Your child will still be able to click on the experience to learn about it, but they won’t have an option to play. Once you feel they’re old enough, you can unblock the experience.

### Manage communication settings

To help minimise contact from harmful strangers, you can customise who your child can communicate with by using Roblox parental controls.

#### To manage chats within experiences:

**Step 1**– From your parent account, go to the **Parental controls menu** > **Communication**. Tap **Experience chat**.

![Screenshot of communication settings in Roblox parental controls.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-communication-settings-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2**– Under **Experience chat**, choose who your child can publicly text chat with. Choose from **Everyone** or **No one**.

Under **Direct chat**, choose **who can send your child a direct message** in Roblox experiences. Choose from Everyone or No one. Note that if you chose ‘No one’ for Experience chat, Direct chat will automatically be No one as well.

![Screenshot showing settings in Roblox Experience chat.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-communication-settings-2-291x300.webp)

#### To manage Party communication:

From the **Communication menu**, tap **Party**.

Under **Party**, select who your child can **form a Party** (up to 2 members) with. Parties are groups which can join experiences together. For children under 13, this is limited to Friends or No one.

Under **Group Party**, choose who **can add your child to a Group Party** (up to 6 members). Again, you can choose between Friends or No one.

Only select Friends if you are across who is in your child’s Friends list.

![Screenshot of Roblox Party chat settings in parental controls.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-communication-settings-3-291x300.webp)

### How to set spending restrictions

Some experiences on Roblox encourage in-game spending. Outside of experiences, there are also various items users can buy for their avatar using Robux. Robux costs real currency, which you can [learn about here](https://roblox.fandom.com/wiki/Robux).

#### To limit spending on Roblox:

**Step 1** – Navigate to the **Parental Controls menu**. Scroll down and tap **Spending restrictions**. Tap **Monthly spending limit**.

![Screenshot showing where to set spending limits with Roblox parental controls.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-spending-limits-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – Enter the **amount you’re happy with** your child spending on a **monthly** basis. Tap **Update**.

If you do not have a credit card set up on their account, they will not be able to spend anything. This limit also does not apply to gift cards.

Note that while the number you enter will save, it might take a few moments to show as updated.

![Screenshot of how to set spending limits with Roblox parental controls.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-spending-limits-2-291x300.webp)

**Step 3** – Go **back** and tap **Spending notifications**. Choose **when you’d like to get notifications** about your child spending on Roblox.

We recommend tracking **all transactions**, particularly if you don’t have spending limits in place.

![Screenshot showing how to set notifications on your child's in-game spending on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-spending-limits-3-291x300.webp)

### How to support your child’s security

There are a range of ways to enhance your child’s privacy and security on Roblox. Doing these steps can help reduce the chance of them being targeted by people hoping to do them harm.

#### To protect your child’s Roblox account:

**Step 1** – In the **Roblox Parental controls menu**, tap **Visibility & private servers** > **Visibility**.

Choose who can **see your child’s Online status** (Friends or No one).

Then, under **Show current experience**, select **who can see which experience/game** your child is currently in on Roblox (Friends or No one).

Unless you personally know the users in their Friends list (such as friends from school), you might want to keep this set to No one.

![Screenshot of Roblox parental controls showing how to manage children's visibility.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-privacy-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2**– Go back and tap **Private servers**. Choose from **Friends and No one** to say who can join your child’s private servers and which private servers they can join.

![Screenshot showing Roblox controls for private servers.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-privacy-2-291x300.webp)

**Step 3** – Go back to the main **Parental controls menu** and tap **Trading & inventory**. Here, you can manage who your child can trade with ([Premium only](https://www.roblox.com/premium/membership)) and who can see their inventory.

We recommend limiting this to **Friends or No one**.

If a stranger can see your child’s inventory and notices there’s an item they want, they might try to manipulate your child to give it to them. That could include convincing your child to give them access to their account.

![Screenshot of Trading and Inventory parental controls on Roblox for premium users.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-privacy-3-291x300.webp)

**Step 4** – From your child’s **Roblox account**, tap **More** > **Settings** > **Security**. Set up **2-Step Verification**. You can choose from:

Tap the **toggle** next to your choice and follow the instructions to set it up. This will help keep your child’s a little more secure, especially if someone else gets access to their password.

![Screenshot showing how to set up two factor authentication on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-privacy-4-291x300.webp)

### Create a private server

Private servers let children play games only with trusted friends they invite, instead of joining public servers with random players. This reduces the risk of interacting with strangers on Roblox.

#### To set up a private server:

**Step 1** – From the **Roblox homepage**, select the game you wish to create a private server for.

![Roblox homepage](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-1-300x148.webp)

**Step 2**– On the page of the game you wish to create a private server for, select **Servers**.

*Note: Some experiences do not allow private servers, so you will need to use a different experience in this case.*

![Roblox game](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-2-300x148.webp)

**Step 3** – Click **Create Private Server**.

![Roblox new private server](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-3-300x141.webp)

**Step 4** – Enter a server name and then select **Buy Now**.

This example is free but some might require robux to purchase.

![Roblox create a private server](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-4-300x147.webp)

**Step 5** – Select **Customize**.

![Roblox customise private server](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-5-300x146.webp)

**Step 6** – On the **Configure Private Server** page, select **Add People.**

![Editing private server Roblox](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-6-300x141.webp)

**Step 7** – Search the username of the account you wish to invite. Select them and then click **Add.**

![Invite to private server Roblox](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-7-300x147.webp)

**Step 8** – The account will now be added to the server. You can view all invited members in the **Server Members** section.

![Roblox invited users](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Roblox-private-servers-8-300x147.webp)

Your child can now play with only their friends on a private server.

### Where to find reporting and blocking tools

Roblox encourages users to block and report users who break rules or make experiences less enjoyable. In addition to blocking specific experiences for your child, your child can use these tools while they play.

Familiarise yourself with how to block and report so that you can show your child to help them take action.

#### To block or report a friend on your child’s account:

From the **Parental Controls menu** in your Roblox app, scroll to **your child’s friends** and tap **Manage**.

Tap the **3 dots** next to the friend. Tap **Block** or **Report** and follow the instructions.

![Screenshot showing how to use Roblox parental controls to block a user on your child's friend's list.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-parental-controls-block-friend-291x300.webp)

#### To block users during a game:

**Step 1** – Tap on the **Roblox icon** in the top left corner. Scroll to find the **user’s name** and then tap the **block icon** (a circle with a line through it).

![Screenshot showing how to block a user while playing a Roblox experience.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-block-in-game-1-300x283.webp)

**Step 2** – Tap **Block**.

If your child needs to also report rule-breaking, the should click **Block and report**. You can then follow the next steps for reporting.

![Screenshot showing blocking options within a Roblox experience.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-block-in-game-2-300x152.webp)

#### To report a user during a game:

**Step 1** – From the same menu you would open to block a user, find the right person and tap the **flag** next to their name.

![Screenshot showing reporting flag highlighted during Roblox game.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-report-in-game-1-300x152.webp)

**Step 2** – Choose from Text Mode or Highlight Mode.

![Screenshot showing Text mode and Highlight mode for in-game reporting on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-report-in-game-2-300x152.webp)

**Step 3a** – In **Text Mode**, select the **Type of Abuse** (chat or avatar) and the **Reason for Abuse** (what your child is reporting the user for).

In the space below, type out **more information** about the abuse and why they’re reporting the user. Tap **Submit**.

![Screenshot of Text Mode reporting in Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-block-in-game-3a-300x152.webp)
![]()

**Step 3b** – In **Highlight Mode**, tap **Enter Highlight Mode**. Place the blue circles (up to 5) **over the examples** that you’re reporting.

Answer **what was wrong**, **where it happened** and **anything else** to help make the report effective. Then tap **Submit**.

![Screenshot of Highlight Mode screens to report users on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-report-in-game-3-300x283.webp)

#### To block or report a user outside a game:

**Step 1** – Open up the **user’s profile**. You can do this by searching for their name or, if they’re in your child’s Friends list, finding them there. Tap the **3 dots** in the bottom left corner. Tap **Report** or **Block**.

![Screenshot showing how to block or report a user on Roblox outside of an experience.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-report-block-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – If **reporting** the user, follow the **instructions** to give Roblox **more information** about why you’re reporting them.

If **blocking** the user, tap **Block** (or **Block and report** if you want to report them as well). To unblock then, tap the **black Unblock button** at the bottom.

If the user was your child’s friend and they wish to have them on their list still, they will need to **send a new friend request**.

![Screenshot showing the report and block options for users on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-report-block-2-291x300.webp)

#### In the unlikely event that your child comes across illegal content:

When **reporting a user**, scroll to the **bottom** of the screen. Tap the link that says **You can also report illegal content under the UK Online Safety Act (UK only)**.

This will open in a browser. **Read through the information** and scroll down to the form. Fully **fill out your contact information**, including your **parent email** rather than your child’s email. Answer the questions and then tap **Submit**.

![Screenshot showing the form to report illegal content on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-illegal-content-291x300.webp)

### How to monitor your teen’s safety

Parents can support their teen’s safety on Roblox with some parental control features to manage screen time and in-game spending.

To start monitoring your teen’s time on Roblox, first [follow these steps to link your account to theirs](#add-parent).

You’ll then be able to review their top experiences, which can help you have conversations around their digital life.

You can also set up [spending alerts](#spending-alerts) so you stay on top of their spending.

### Help your teen build trusted connections

While parental controls support under-13s, teens have their own tools to keep themselves safe. Trusted Connections offer greater communication options that might be restricted with normal interactions.

#### To set up Trusted Connections:

**Step 1** – On your **teen’s account** (with your teen), go to **More** > **Settings** > **Account Info**. Tap **Verify My Age** and follow the verification instructions.

![Screenshot of press images from Roblox's teen age verification feature.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-trusted-connection-1-291x300.webp)

**Step 2** – Age-checked users that your teen adds through a QR code or from their Contacts list will become a Trusted Connection. Your child can review this via their **Friends list**.

![Press images showcasing the Trusted Connection feature for teens on Roblox.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/roblox-trusted-connection-2-291x300.webp)

# [Introducing Updates to Our Safety Protections and Parental Controls](/t/introducing-updates-to-our-safety-protections-and-parental-controls/3264200)

### Key Takeaways

Hi Creators,

Today, we are sharing the latest updates to our safety controls, including significant improvements to parental controls, how users under age 13 can communicate on Roblox, new content labels, and built-in protections for younger users. Before we dive in, here is a reminder of the latest updates to our content maturity policies:

# Reminder of our Updated Content Maturity Policies

In July, we [announced a change](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/upcoming-changes-to-experience-guidelines/3070343) to our default content maturity settings for users under 9 years old. **Starting today, users under the age of 9 will only be able to access experiences with a content label of “Minimal” or “Mild” by default.** Parents can use parental controls to let their children access more mature content.

As a reminder, we’ve added the ability to see what percent of your audience is under 9 years old, to help you better understand the impact these changes will have on your experience(s). You can access this new functionality in Creator Hub under [Analytics](https://create.roblox.com/dashboard/analytics).

[![](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/original/5X/0/1/3/d/013ddea46455270bfdfa46d8afb7e3ea134ce4c6.png)

619×275 8.55 KB](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/original/5X/0/1/3/d/013ddea46455270bfdfa46d8afb7e3ea134ce4c6.png)

![](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/original/5X/0/1/3/d/013ddea46455270bfdfa46d8afb7e3ea134ce4c6.png)

Additionally, to help provide parents and users more clarity into the types of content available on Roblox, we’ve begun labeling experiences based on the type of content users can expect in an experience, rather than by age. Experience Guidelines are now called Content Labels, which is reflected in the questionnaire you fill out for your experience. “Age Guidelines” is now called “Content Maturity”, and users will continue to be able to customize their access to experiences based on their Content Maturity setting under Parental Controls. The new content labels are now Minimal, Mild, Moderate, and Restricted.

You can find more information about these updates [here](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/upcoming-changes-to-experience-guidelines/3070343).

### Users under the age of 13 will not be able to join, search, and discover experiences without content maturity labels.

We recently published [updated policy guidance](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/updating-experience-guideline-policies-to-keep-our-younger-users-safe/3249079) for our experience questionnaire. If you have not already, please remember to fill out the updated experience questionnaire by **December 3, 2024**; otherwise,your experience will not be accessible for users under 13. All experiences without content maturity labels will be filtered out of search and any public or recommended sorts for users under 13. Go to [Creator Hub](https://create.roblox.com/) > Creations then select an experience and go to Audience > Questionnaire to complete it.

### Restricting social hangouts and free-form user creation to users 13+

**Starting today**, experiences with certain types of interactive features, specifically social hangouts and free-form 2D user creation, will only be accessible to users over the age of 13. Please review the previous [DevForum announcement](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/updating-experience-guideline-policies-to-keep-our-younger-users-safe/3249079) for more information.

# New and Revised Parental Controls

We’re also announcing new and improved parental controls to provide more tools and visibility to parents over their child’s experience on Roblox.

### Accounts with parent privileges

**Today** we’re launching remote management for parents, which allows parents and caregivers to adjust parental controls and review their child’s activity from their own accounts. Parents who want to be more involved in monitoring their child’s activities can link their Roblox account to their child’s account after verifying themselves using an ID or credit card. After linking accounts, parents can manage their child’s experience and access from Parental Controls.

[![Link to your child](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/optimized/5X/c/e/7/9/ce793cac6d033e5ccefd1828d1a04b64601d5ad1_2_178x375.png)

Link to your child834×1752 168 KB](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/original/5X/c/e/7/9/ce793cac6d033e5ccefd1828d1a04b64601d5ad1.png "Link to your child")

![Link to your child](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/optimized/5X/c/e/7/9/ce793cac6d033e5ccefd1828d1a04b64601d5ad1_2_178x375.png)

### Friends list and screen-time monitoring

In the Parental Controls dashboard, parents can now see their child’s screen time over the past week, as well as their child’s friends list. Parents can also set daily screen-time limits for their child.

[![Parental controls dashboard](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/optimized/5X/b/e/e/7/bee7288e47173d44a93e6c7a37bbae9824a90b62_2_178x375.png)

Parental controls dashboard834×1752 91.2 KB](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/original/5X/b/e/e/7/bee7288e47173d44a93e6c7a37bbae9824a90b62.png "Parental controls dashboard")

![Parental controls dashboard](//devforum-uploads.s3.dualstack.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/uploads/optimized/5X/b/e/e/7/bee7288e47173d44a93e6c7a37bbae9824a90b62_2_178x375.png)

### Reminder about updates to the Roblox parent PIN

As previously announced over email, as of today, you are no longer able to set or use a parent PIN on your Roblox account. As always, if you are interested in an added layer of security on your account, you can [set up 2-factor authentication](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/212459863-Add-2-Step-Verification-to-Your-Account).

# Updates to our Communication Settings

Connecting with others is core to the Roblox experience, and we want to facilitate that with safety in mind. Over the next few months, we are adding new limitations and parental controls around how children under age 13 can communicate on the platform to add additional protections for our youngest users.

As we previously announced, we’ve [removed](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/sunsetting-user-to-user-inbox-messaging/3187502?page=3) the ability for users to message each other via the Roblox Inbox and are removing the legacy chat system by **April 30**. The primary reason for this change is to better ensure that all chat messages between users respect our privacy settings and parental controls. For more information about the legacy chat system change, you can read the prior DevForum announcement [here](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/migrate-to-textchatservice-removing-support-for-legacy-chat-and-custom-chat-systems/3237100).

In addition, **users under the age of 13 will no longer able to directly message others on Roblox outside of games or experiences (also known as platform chat)**. When communicating in a game or experience, users under the age of 13 will be able to communicate using the broadcast public chat. To use direct messaging within experiences, users under 13 will need parental consent.

# Next Steps

As a reminder, **please do the following 2 things**:

**Remember to fill out the experience questionnaire by December 3, 2024**; otherwise, your experience will not be accessible to users under 13. If your experience contains any content that may be relevant to free-form user creation and social hangouts, you must re-take the questionnaire or your maturity label could be removed. However, if your experience is not impacted by the policy updates and does not contain content that relates to the descriptors, you do not need to update your answers and your maturity label will not be removed. We are looking into product updates to make it easier to answer just the new questions of the questionnaire.

**For those using forked legacy chat system or custom chat: Remember to integrate with [CanUserDirectChatAsync](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/integrate-textchatservicecanusersdirectchatasync-or-textchannelsetdirectchatrequester-api-to-comply-with-settings/3255672) API by January 30th, 2025.** This API checks whether a user can receive or send direct chats. For experiences that do not implement this API by this deadline, we will attempt to automatically migrate experiences that do not comply. If that is unsuccessful, we’ll attempt to disable chat for those experiences until the experience is migrated to TextChatService. As a last resort, in the case of custom chat implementations that do not use either legacy chat system or TextChatService, we may need to restrict access to your experience to only you and notify you that you will need to manually remove your chat integration and integrate TextChatService to restore your experience.

# Parental Controls FAQ

## What are Parental Controls on Roblox?

Use Parental Controls on Roblox to choose how your child engages and interacts with others across Roblox. You can make informed decisions about what is right for your family and manage your child’s account features, such as their daily screen time, on-platform friends, and Robux balance.

## How do I manage parental controls for my child’s account?

There are two ways to manage parental controls for your child:

Learn more in the [Parents: How to Link Your Account](/hc/en-us/articles/30428321333140) help article.

## What is Parent mode?

Parent mode lets you approve your child’s requests and manage their settings on their device, without your own Roblox account. When your child makes a request, they can select **Ask in Person** and give you their device. You verify that you’re an adult, review the request, and create a 6-digit PIN to approve future requests faster.

Parent mode is rolling out gradually and may not be available to everyone yet.

## What’s the difference between Parent mode and a linked parent account?

Both let you approve your child’s requests and change their settings. With a linked parent account, you can also:

You can set up a linked parent account at any time, even after using Parent mode.

## Can I use Parent mode if I already have a linked parent account?

Not right now. Parent mode is only available for children who don’t have a linked parent account. If your account is linked to your child’s, manage their settings from your own device in **Settings** > **Parental Controls**.

## What is a linked parent account?

A linked parent account on Roblox allows you to approve certain actions for your child on Roblox. You can also explore Roblox as an avatar on your own or with your child. When creating a linked parent account, you’ll be asked to enter your birthday, verify your age through facial age estimation or using a government-issued ID or credit card, and link to your child’s account.

## Who can create a linked parent account?

In most regions, parents of children under 18 can create and link a parent account to their child's account. To create a linked parent account, you must be age checked 18 years of age or older.

## What if I already have a Roblox account?

If you already have a Roblox account, you can link it to your child’s account and add parent privileges. Learn more in the [Parents: How to Link Your Account help article.](/hc/en-us/articles/30428321333140)

## Why do I need a different Roblox account from my child’s account?

Not always. If your child doesn’t have a linked parent account, you can use **Parent mode** to approve requests and manage most settings on their device.

Having your own account linked to your child’s account allows you to manage your child’s experience from your own device without the need to log into your child’s account every time you want to make a change or view insights. You also get emails about your child’s activity, such as spending notifications.

## How do I unlink from a child account?

To unlink from a child account, go to **Settings** > **Parental Controls**, and select the child you want to unlink from. Select the **pencil** **icon** in the top right corner, and then select **Unlink** **accounts**. Note that if you unlink your account from your child’s, you will no longer be able to provide permission for actions on Roblox, control their privacy settings, set screen time or spending limits, view their Robux balance, or add Robux to their account.

## What settings can I manage for my child?

You can manage your child’s content, chat, spending settings, and more. The settings you can manage depend on your child’s age. As your child gets older, some settings move from you to your child, but you can still view insights and manage select settings.

If you use Parent mode, you can manage most settings on your child’s device, except settings that send you real-time alerts, such as spending notifications. These need a linked parent account.

For details on which settings you can manage at each age, see the [What happens as my child or teen gets older on Roblox?](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/30428367965460) help article.

We also recommend checking out these help articles:

## Can I allow or block my child from playing specific games?

You can control your child’s access to certain games, regardless of their content maturity labels, using the [Allowed or blocked games](/hc/en-us/articles/30428310121620#h_01JP88T3VENG6Y2C9DKAGAYTNQ) feature in Parental Controls. You can also view your child's [top games played](/hc/en-us/articles/30428328969492#h_01JQFMQBBME8XJR5EY9V6F4R73) and block games directly.

## Can I see my child's Robux balance?

Yes. If your account is linked to your child's, you can see their Robux balance in **Settings** > **Parental Controls**. This is available for all linked children. Learn more in the [Parental Controls Overview](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/30428310121620#robux-balance) help article.

## Can I add Robux to my child's account?

Yes. You can add Robux to your linked child's account from **Settings** > **Parental Controls**. Learn more in the [Parental Controls Overview](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/30428310121620#robux-balance) help article.

## Why am I being asked for parental consent?

If you receive an email to provide parental consent for your child on Roblox, this is because your child needs your permission to take certain actions on Roblox. You will need a Roblox account with parent privileges to provide consent for your child.

## Can I share my account with parent privileges?

We understand partners, friends and siblings may want to share their Roblox accounts. Roblox does not encourage account sharing. Anyone with access to your account can make changes to sensitive information on the account, including changes to your linked child accounts. Roblox accounts are free to make, and multiple parents can link to the same child's account from their own different accounts.

## What happens when my child grows older?

Children’s settings will be updated when they reach certain ages, if they and their parents haven’t previously made changes to them. Learn more in the [What happens as I get older on Roblox](/hc/en-us/articles/30428367965460) help article.

## How do I deactivate my child’s Roblox account?

You can deactivate your child’s account from **Settings** > **Privacy & content maturity** on their account. Check out our help article, [How do I deactivate or delete my account](/hc/en-us/articles/203313050) to learn more about deactivating or deleting your child’s Roblox account.
